newsitem.title: CHINA: China population birth rate falls in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China population birth rate falls in 1996.

text.p: The birth rate in China, the world's most populous country with 1.2 billion people, fell slightly to 17 per 1,000 in 1996, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
Last year's figure compared with 17.12 per 1,000 in 1995. The 1995 rate was the equivalent 470,000 fewer births than in 1994, earlier reports said.

China has imposed a strict one-couple, one-child family planning policy to try to control the growth of its population, which reached 1.2 billion at the end of 1995 and could swell to 1.3 billion by the turn of the century.

China launched its birth control policy in 1979 when its population neared one billion after 20 years of promotion of big families by Chairman Mao Zedong, who believed a large population could make China strong.
China fines urban families that have more than one child, but has relaxed its policy slightly in rural areas.
Beijing has come under fire from human rights groups and foreign governments who accused it of using forced abortions and sterilisations to check its population.
China denies such charges, and says it must feed 22 percent of the world's population on just seven percent of its arable land.
